names.name: Krispy Kreme
names.said: The name is a deliberate misspelling of crispy cream, and it has been for ninety years.

text.what: The Winston-Salem company built on a bought yeast-raised recipe, a window you can watch the line through, and a lit sign.
text.story: Vernon Rudolph bought the recipe from a New Orleans chef and rented a building in 1937 in what is now historic Old Salem. Steady growth ran to an expansion as a public company between 2000 and 2016 that proved unprofitable; JAB Holding took it private in 2016; it listed again on the Nasdaq in July 2021. Headquarters moved to Charlotte in December 2017, with most operations left in Winston-Salem. A group of franchisees had bought the company back from Beatrice Foods in 1982, ten years after Beatrice acquired it.
text.today: The early-2010s tunnel-oven shops keep the hot sign lit all day, which is a different promise from the one the sign made in 1937.
